purpose: Ledgerline PR4, 'Results and docs': anyone can open a Results page and see how Ledgerline scored on every benchmark schema, with plain-English metric definitions, intervals, the simulated label and links to the triage files. The repo documents itself for a newcomer: a README walk-through, a product brief, ADR results, a build log and triaged failures. It also lands the small fixes filed from PR3.
mechanism:
1. ledgerline/bench/report_schema.py defines the report shape as Pydantic models (extra='forbid', rates between 0 and 1); evals/report.schema.json is generated from it and tests/bench/test_report_schema.py checks the committed file equals the generated one and every committed report validates.
2. ledgerline/bench/results.py adds GET /api/reports (every committed report, most schemas first), GET /api/reports/{id} (one report plus the schemas that have a triage file) and GET /api/triage/{schema} (plain text); only ids found by listing evals/reports/*.json and evals/triage/*.yaml are opened. ledgerline/api.py installs these routes.
3. web/results/index.html and web/src/results.ts are a second Vite page at /results/: a report picker, the status under the title, a banner (simulated, measured with a real model only when status is complete, otherwise 'Not measured' and the status), per-schema tables with one row per system and model, seven metric definitions, the floor verdict, miss rows and triage links; all text set through the h() helper, never innerHTML. web/vite.config.ts builds both pages; web/src/main.ts links to Results.
4. ledgerline/bench/report.py: the Markdown heading reads '(v0.1 acceptance floor)'; evals/reports/*.md regenerated by replay; evals/floors.yaml comment plain.
5. ledgerline/workspace/rules.py: decimals with more than 17 significant digits (zeros at either end not counted) are long_num; money and percent patterns accept U+00A0 and U+202F as spaces, and number_fix strips them. ledgerline/workspace/check.py: a blank header no longer hides a duplicate-name report.
6. verify.sh comment carries the same Chromium install command as the README.
7. Docs: README walk-through (at most 600 words before '## Setup details', checked by tests/test_docs.py), docs/product-brief.md, ADR Result lines, docs/build-log.md, docs/failures/ (fs-022, fs-025, fs-028, fs-035, fieldservice only).
decisions: Pydantic models generate the JSON Schema instead of adding jsonschema as a dependency (rejected: a new dev dependency for one test). The results routes list folders and open only listed names (rejected: building a path from the request). Failures use fieldservice only because Spider question text must never be committed. The README and brief say v0.1 refuses what the validator rejects, but a question outside the grammar can still get a wrong answer (3 of the 43 answerable fieldservice questions in sim-1).
readers: README, docs/product-brief.md and docs/failures: users and hiring managers reading the repo. docs/adr and docs/build-log.md: engineers judging the design. Code comments and docstrings: the next maintainer.
